Dataojitori/horon.description: Executable memory & cognitive harness for AI agents. Let your agent learn, remember, and build its own guardrails.
Dataojitori/horon.body:
**Executable memory for AI agents — turn what an agent learns into attention paths, stateful logic, and tool-level guardrails.**

> **Let AI build redstone circuits out of the losses it has suffered, circuits that stop it from repeating them.**

---

## What it can build

- **Adaptive memory**: Horon learns the paths along which the AI actually browses its memory. After reading A, it often needs B next; the next time A is read, B is more likely to be surfaced right in front of it.
- **Automated circuits**: Chain “finish A before doing B” and “when you see X, remind yourself” into circuits that trigger automatically.
- **Physical brakes**: When a precondition is not met, block the tool before it executes and tell the AI which step is still missing.
- **Reusable patterns (Tag plugins)**: Like industrial molds, write the “correct way” of handling a class of tasks as a plugin. New tasks that get attached a tag are automatically bound by that approach.

## See it in action

1. **Catching verbal promises on the spot**: The AI verbally agrees in conversation with “Got it, I’ve noted that,” but never actually calls a tool to write to the database. Horon intercepts it on the spot and reports: *“You said you noted it, but nothing was written this turn.”*

2. **Email reply pipeline**:
   - Supplier Xiaolin sends a routine confirmation email. The system triggers a sensor and shows a reminder: *“【Horon Harness】Message received from Xiaolin. Please read ‘Guidelines for writing to Xiaolin’ (ID 482), then compose a reply.”*
   - The AI tries to call `send_email` directly without reading? **Blocked**: *“You haven’t read ‘Guidelines for writing to Xiaolin’ yet. Finish reading before sending.”*
   - After reading, the system automatically runs a check: Are there AI boilerplate phrases such as “值得注意的是” (“it is worth noting that”)? Is the recipient correct? Only when everything passes is the circuit powered and the send allowed.

3. **Preventing public posting mistakes**:
   - The AI autonomously posts or replies on a social platform, and the draft accidentally includes a real name, private chat logs, or an API key.
   - The send tool is **cut off** before execution: *“Sensitive private information detected; external sending is prohibited.”*

**You don’t need to build the circuits yourself.** Tell your AI what you need, and have it build the mechanisms by following Horon’s manual (skill).

> [!WARNING]
> **Horon is still in early development.** Updates may break existing data, and circuits your AI has already built may stop working as a result.

## Installation

You don’t have to do it yourself. Send the following to your AI:

```text
Please help me install Horon: read https://github.com/Dataojitori/horon/blob/master/docs/INSTALL.md and follow it.
```

Supports **Claude Code**, **Codex**, **Antigravity**, **OpenCode**, and **DeepSeek Harness**.

## iOS App Maintenance

Free Apple ID signing typically expires after 7 days. When the app won't open after expiration, reconnect the iPhone and press `Cmd + R` in Xcode to reinstall and renew the signing for 7 more days:

```bash
cd /Users/max/Desktop/github/interview
source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22
npx cap open ios
```

If you're only renewing the signing without changing content, you don't need to rebuild the web artifacts.

If you've modified the blog content, you need to rebuild and sync first:

```bash
cd /Users/max/Desktop/github/interview

source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 16.19.1
MOBILE=1 npm run docs:build

source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22.22.2
npx cap sync ios
npx cap open ios
```

Then select iPhone in Xcode and press `Cmd + R` to install.

Local image and video processing · Real-time window enhancement. Adjust and compare visuals in one workspace.

This document describes the **v3.1.0** local packaged build, which improves super-resolution processing, automatic pre-rendering, cache reclamation, and export efficiency, and adds queued output directory management. chinjiaqing/jc-daily-report.description: Daily football match analysis for Jingcai (China's sports lottery), with interpretation of football betting handicaps; football lottery
chinjiaqing/jc-daily-report.body:
# ⚽ Football Signal Radar · Daily Signal Report

> **Set emotion aside and watch only the signals.**
> Three-channel cross-validation of handicap movements. No bets at low odds, no bets when the signal is unclear. Pre-match execution is automatic, and settlement after the match is automatic.

## 🚀 Online Site

- **[https://chinjiaqing.github.io/jc-daily-report/](https://chinjiaqing.github.io/jc-daily-report/)**
- Updated automatically every hour, with historical dates archived so you can look back at any time
- Covers **500 to 1300+** matches per day (full Jingcai/Asian handicap coverage), with automatic signal and bet tagging

---

## The Detours We Bypassed

We tried **models**. We stacked up parameters until the room was full. Looking back, the models only repeated the prices the market had already set. No matter how many parameters we added, nothing new came out.

We tried **studying the bookmakers**. We kept guessing at the operators' moves, and the more we guessed, the more it looked like paranoid delusion. In the end we realized: guessing at the house is less useful than watching the price.

We also tried **AI prediction**: injuries, motivation, form. Every point was argued convincingly, and every point had already been priced into the odds long before. However loud the argument, the handicap doesn't accept it.

After these detours, one plain principle remains:

> **Money shows where it is going, and the handicap speaks.**
> But people watching the board get carried away easily: chasing favorites, fearing upsets, and shaky hands near kickoff. You can see at a glance when emotion is doing the trading.

So we hand both "watching" and "buying" to the machine, and people keep only one thing: **discipline**.

## Three Informants, One Referee

**1X2 odds** track market-wide odds movements: who has been collectively abandoned, who is quietly defending, and whether the draw line has been given up. This is the informant closest to the action.

**Asian handicap** tracks the handicap line and water levels: sudden pivots near kickoff, and the sniping of upper-side money. The money is real, thrown down in real cash, and more honest than what people say.

**Over/Under** tracks the total goals line: once a goal-rich setup appears, the number of goals in the match has often already been signaled.

Each of the three informants has its own news. When the news agrees, the referee dares to rule. **Matches where the signals disagree (1X2 and Asian handicap fighting each other) are not touched at all.** If the informants are already arguing among themselves, there is no reason for you to place a bet.

## Discipline Matters More Than Vision

Once the direction is set, everything left is discipline:

- **No bets at low odds**: a single-selection price below 1.5, or a double-selection price below 1.3 after discounting, is not bought even with a good signal. At odds that low, even a win doesn't earn much.
- **No bets when the signal is unclear**: no signal, conflicting signals, or a vague direction means wait and watch in every case. Missing out doesn't lose money. Betting wrongly does.
- **Quality determines stake size**: the stronger the signal, the larger the stake (1/2/4 units). No all-in gambling.
- **Bets are placed automatically 15 minutes before kickoff, and results are settled automatically when they come in**: no shaky hands near kickoff, and no urge to raise stakes after a win or chase losses after a defeat.

---

## ⚠️ Disclaimer

This project is for data research only and does not constitute any purchase advice. Buy lottery tickets only at physical retail outlets offline. Persons under 18 years of age may not participate.

hloolx/codpl.body:
# CODPL

CODPL is a static benchmark site for multi-vendor Coding Plan / Code API services. It supports Coding Plan evaluation, Coding Plan speed testing, Code API benchmarking, multi-vendor model comparison, and long-term trend tracking. The project continuously displays TTFT, MedianTPS, composite experience scores, and historical snapshots for different platforms and models, so developers can review real probe results before onboarding, purchasing, or model selection.

If you are searching for any of the following, this project is for you:

- Coding Plan evaluation
- Coding Plan benchmark
- Coding Plan speed test
- Coding Plan vendor comparison
- Coding Plan purchase reference
- Code API response speed comparison
- TTFT / MedianTPS / composite experience rankings

## Live Sites

- Main site: <https://codpl.15o.cc>
- Overseas node: <https://bench.codpl.com/>
- Vendor onboarding status, purchase links, and official documentation entry points: <https://bench.codpl.com/providers>

The overseas node is served by Cloudflare and is suited to access from overseas networks.

## What the Project Does

- Continuously probes multiple Coding Plan / Code API vendors and publicly displays the latest round of results.
- Compares time to first token (TTFT), MedianTPS, composite scores, and the performance of the same model across vendors.
- Stores historical data as static JSON snapshots, making it easy to observe 24-hour and 30-day trend changes.
- Provides developers, team buyers, and model selectors with a public, intuitive, and verifiable reference page.

This repository is the frontend release repository. It keeps only the frontend code and snapshot data needed by the static site, and does not include backend source code, databases, or private environment variables.

## Vendors Currently Covered by Probing

The current public page covers the following Coding Plan / Code API vendors. For the full model list, see [BENCHMARK_COVERAGE.md](https://github.com/hloolx/codpl/blob/HEAD/BENCHMARK_COVERAGE.md):

# IOTA Watch

An open-source, five-language, multi-project monitoring dashboard centered on **IOTA Train at Home**. It supports IOTA, XID / MMM, Quantus, fly.ai, Nosana, Gonka, Akash, io.net, Vast.ai and Golem; each project's inputs, cycles, and data coverage are described separately.

**[Official site](https://iotahome.site) · [My Devices](https://iotahome.site/zh/devices) · [IOTA Lookup](https://iotahome.site/zh/app) · [Network Status](https://iotahome.site/zh/network) · [Blog](https://iotahome.site/zh/blog) · [English](https://iotahome.site/en)**

IOTA Watch is an independent MIT-licensed monitor in English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Korean and Japanese. nitr0yukkuri/githubplanet.description: A web app that visualizes GitHub activity data as user-specific 3D planets, achievements, and real-time meteors.
nitr0yukkuri/githubplanet.body:
> GitHub Planet is an open-source interactive project that is not affiliated with GitHub.

## What is GitHub Planet?

GitHub Planet represents a developer's GitHub activity as a 3D planet floating in space. It aggregates the language composition of owned public repositories, contributions, Stars, contributions to external repositories, and so on, and reflects the results in the planet's color, surface, size, rotation, surrounding stars, and achievements. Pinned representative works on GitHub are separated from the planet-wide language aggregation, and the languages of each work are shown individually. Language ratios represent the composition of the entire repository, not the ratio of only the code the user added.

The heart of this project is not a list of numbers. It lets you rotate a planet that reflects your own development history to observe its surface textures and per-language expression, and compare it with the planets of other developers.

## 🏆 Awards

- **CSS Winner Star** (Score 7.5) — https://www.csswinner.com/details/github-planet/19334
- **Demo Stage** Grand Prize
- **技育CAMP Vol.14** Excellence Award
- **技育博 Vol.6** Corporate Award (ウイングアーク1st)
- **ヒーローズ・リーグ 2025** Finalist

## 🎬 Try it in 1 minute

[Open the demo (no login required)](https://githubplanet.dev/demo?showcase=typescript)

1. Open the demo
2. Look at the planet's color, surface, size, and rotation
3. Check the achievements and per-language expression
4. Switch between language showcases to compare

This demo uses fixed data and does not depend on real GitHub users or the production database.

## Main features

- **Your own planet:** Generates a distinctive planet based on activity data obtained through GitHub OAuth.
- **3D observation:** Displays the planet in 3D with Three.js / WebGL so you can rotate it, and check language composition, contributions, and titles in the status drawer.
- **Language-specific expression:** For each language, switches not only the sphere color but also the surface material, shaders, outer shell, wind, sand dust, crystals, and more.
- **Space exploration:** Search by username or visit randomly to observe the saved planets of other users.
- **Real-time meteors:** Delivers GitHub Push Webhook events over Socket.IO, and displays meteor color and size according to the changed languages and the amount of change.

# 🚀 Docker Image Toolbox: Build and Sync

This project is a collection of GitHub Actions workflows, designed to provide a one-stop Docker image management solution.

It mainly includes two core features:

1. **Build multi-architecture images from Git repositories**: Pull the source code of any Git repository, automatically build Docker images supporting multiple CPU architectures (such as `amd64`, `arm64`), and push them to Docker Hub and GitHub Packages (`ghcr.io`).
2. **Sync public images to speed up downloads**: Sync images from public registries such as Docker Hub to your own `ghcr.io` repository, to speed up image pulls in mainland China and other regions. If `ghcr.io` speed is still unsatisfactory, it can be used together with the Nanjing University acceleration site `ghcr.nju.edu.cn`.

## ✨ Key Features

- **Dual core**: Combines image **building** and **syncing** in one, meeting needs in different scenarios.
- **Manual trigger**: All workflows can be started manually from the Actions page via a simple form.
- **Multi-architecture support**: Easily build images for `linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`, `linux/arm/v7`, and other CPU architectures.
- **Multi-registry push**: Build once and automatically push the image to GitHub Packages (`ghcr.io`) and Docker Hub.
- **Automatic updates**: Synced images get a daily automatic update mechanism, ensuring the version you use is always up to date.
- **Automated results**: After a successful workflow run, the image list in this `README.md` file is automatically updated.
- **Secure and reliable**: Manages your private credentials securely through GitHub's encrypted Secrets, avoiding the risk of hardcoding.

## 🛠️ First-Time Installation and Configuration

For all features to work properly, the safest and most recommended approach is to **Fork this project** into your own GitHub account, then complete the following one-time configuration.

yaklang/OpenXDR.body:
# OpenXDR

Chinese | [English](https://github.com/yaklang/OpenXDR/blob/HEAD/README.en.md)

Open-source XDR platform: EDR + SIEM + full-traffic analysis, with AI-driven noise reduction and operations.

**Managing a host is operating it; managing a host is securing it.** Install an agent on a host and put it in a group, and it automatically gets continuous collection, detection, daily inspections, and a conversational AI assistant. People make the decisions and no longer dig through alert lists.

**Noise stops here; what remains is worth a look.**

## What it can do

- **Onboard a host with one command**: The console issues onboarding tokens per group. One command installs the agent on Linux (x86_64 / arm64) or Windows. The host generates its private key locally, and the server issues a host-binding certificate. Afterward, drop a new build into the distribution directory and online agents upgrade automatically, without logging into the hosts again. Existing operations documents can be imported directly. Credentials are stored encrypted, and SSH management is authorized per group.
- **Collection that works in any environment**: processes, files, persistence points, login and security logs, outbound network connections, and kernel modules. eBPF / ETW are optional. When unavailable, collection automatically falls back to netlink, fanotify, or polling, preferring weaker collection over fabricated data. The full-traffic probe emits only session metadata (DNS / TLS JA3 and certificates / HTTP) and does not store PCAP. Syslog ingestion is also supported.
- **Layered noise reduction**: Sigma-compatible rules (hot-reloaded; the ATT&CK matrix highlights gaps where “a rule exists but no data source”), threat intelligence matching (built-in public feeds such as abuse.ch), persistent deduplication, reversible false-positive suppression, event graphs correlated by entity, and UEBA first-seen detection. Finally, AI with investigation tools actively triages. Low-risk benign events are automatically closed when they expire, and anything needing human review is always left to people. Time-series detection (count and sequence rules, in a separate directory, explicitly enabled, under development) is also available.
- **Software vulnerabilities**: Agents report the dpkg software inventory, and the server checks it against the OSV vulnerability database. It flags vulnerabilities that can be fixed by upgrading and the affected externally exposed services. Offline vulnerability databases are supported. Currently only Debian / Ubuntu are covered.
- **Identity correlation** (under development): Normalizes Linux / Windows logins and local accounts, and can sync directory accounts from Keycloak, Entra ID, and AD / LDAP. Accounts with the same name are not merged across devices until the directory's authority is verified.
- **Asset graph and attack surface**: Agents report listening ports and cloud environments, and connection relationships are aggregated into a dependency graph. AI labels each asset's role, function, and importance (manually editable and lockable). Assets are automatically grouped into intranet, quarantine zone, public zone, or cloud by subnet, cloud environment, and IP. Each externally exposed service is ranked by exposure level × port risk × importance. Machines that have connected but are not under management are listed as blind spots.
- **AI assistant and inspections**: Operations through conversation. The AI can run commands on hosts within a group, query the database through read-only group views, register operations to-dos, …
